sections.h2: Inflatable hire for every kind of event
sections.html:
From an adult bouncy castle or laser tag arena to a 220ft obstacle course, rodeo bull and a field full of inflatable games for a corporate fun day, JM Inflatable Hire has the stock and the crew to make it happen. Everything you see on this site is our own stock, kept in our own warehouse and set up by our own team.

Every hire includes delivery, professional set-up, a full safety check and collection. Add operators and staff so your guests are looked after all day, or combine inflatables with arcade games, simulators and side stalls from the wider JM Entertainment range.

• Huge range in one place – castles, slides, assault courses, games, challenges and rodeo rides.
  • Live stock and availability straight from our booking system, so you know what's free before you call.
  • Fixed, clear pricing with multi-day discounts shown on every product.
  • Safety first – PIPA-tested inflatables, PAT-tested blowers and trained, DBS-checked crew.
  • Nationwide coverage for corporate events, schools, councils, festivals and private parties.
  • Fully insured, with risk assessments supplied once you've booked.

sections.h2: Popular for corporate fun days, schools and festivals
sections.html: Our inflatables are booked for staff summer parties, family fun days, team building, school sports days and summer fairs, university freshers' events, shopping-centre activations, council events, festivals, weddings and birthday parties. Mix and match – assault course races, a Gladiators duel and a rodeo bull together make a brilliant It's-a-Knockout style day.

faq.q: How much does inflatable hire cost?
faq.a: Adult bouncy castles start from around £125 + VAT per day, inflatable games and challenges from around £175–£695 + VAT, and showpieces such as assault courses, Wipeout, bungee runs, laser tag and bumper cars from around £450–£1,995 + VAT. Delivery, set-up and collection are included on most UK bookings, and multi-day hires are discounted – each product page shows 1, 2, 3, 4 and 7-day prices.

faq.q: Do you deliver inflatables nationwide?
faq.a: Yes. Our crews deliver, set up and collect across England, Scotland and Wales – from London and the South East to Manchester, Birmingham, Leeds, Newcastle, Glasgow and Cardiff.

faq.q: What power do inflatables need?
faq.a: Most inflatables run from one standard 13 amp socket within 25 metres for the electric blower. No power on site? We can supply a petrol blower or generator – just ask when you book.

faq.q: Can inflatables be used outdoors on grass?
faq.a: Yes – grass is ideal. We stake every inflatable down and supply safety mats. On hard ground or indoors we use sandbags and crash mats instead. Inflatables can't be used in high winds or heavy rain, so our crew will advise on the day.

faq.q: Are your inflatables safety tested?
faq.a: Every inflatable is PIPA tested, cleaned and checked before each hire, and all blowers are PAT tested. We hold public liability insurance; risk assessments and insurance documents are supplied once your booking is confirmed.

news.title: How JM Inflatable Hire Follows the PIPA Safety Scheme
news.meta: How JM Inflatable Hire follows the PIPA inflatable inspection scheme – annual tests to BS EN 14960, numbered PIPA tags you can check, and our safety checks on every hire.
news.summary: Every inflatable we hire is part of the PIPA inspection scheme. Here is what that means, what we do before every hire and how you can check our tags yourself.
news.html:
When you hire an inflatable, you are trusting the supplier with your guests' safety. That's why JM Inflatable Hire follows the PIPA scheme – the UK inspection scheme for inflatable play equipment – and why we're happy to show you the paperwork for anything you book.

What is PIPA?

PIPA (the Pertinent Inflatable Patrons Association) runs the UK's inspection and tagging scheme for inflatable play equipment. Each inflatable in the scheme is inspected by a PIPA-registered inspector against the European safety standard for inflatable play equipment, BS EN 14960. When it passes, it is given a numbered PIPA tag and the test is logged on PIPA's national database.

The Health and Safety Executive (HSE) advises anyone hiring a bouncy castle or play inflatable to check that it has either a numbered PIPA tag or an ADIPS Declaration of Compliance, and written evidence that it complies with BS EN 14960.

How we follow the scheme

  • Annual inspection. Our inflatables are inspected every year by a PIPA-registered inspector, and each one carries its own numbered tag.
  • Checked before every hire. Between hires every inflatable is cleaned, dried and checked for rips, seam damage and worn anchor points, and the blower is checked too. Electrical equipment is PAT tested.
  • Anchored properly. We use every anchor point on the inflatable. On grass we use steel stakes; on tarmac, concrete or indoors we use heavy ballast instead, following HSE guidance.
  • Weather limits. We don't operate inflatables in winds above 24mph (Force 5) – or the lower limit in the manufacturer's manual where there is one – and our crew check the wind on site.
  • Safe-use briefing. Before we leave, we brief the person supervising on the rules for that inflatable: user numbers, ages and heights, no shoes or sharp objects, and what to do if the weather changes. Or add our operators and we'll supervise for you.
  • Paperwork for your venue. Once you've booked, we send our insurance certificate, risk assessment, method statement and PIPA details for your venue, school or council.

How to check a PIPA tag yourself

  1. Ask us for the PIPA tag number of the inflatable you're booking – or find the tag, usually attached near the entrance or blower tube.
  2. Enter the number on the PIPA website, pipa.org.uk.
  3. Check the photo and description match the inflatable, and that the test date is within the last 12 months.

If anything doesn't match, don't use the inflatable – and with us, just call and we'll sort it out straight away.

Questions?

Ask for the PIPA tag numbers for any inflatable on your quote, or read our safety FAQs. You can also browse the full range on our inflatable hire page.

news.title: What Is a PIPA Tag? A Plain-English Guide for Anyone Hiring an Inflatable
news.meta: What a PIPA tag is, what it proves, how to check one at pipa.org.uk, and the difference between PIPA and ADIPS – a simple guide for parents, schools and event organisers.
news.summary: Booking a bouncy castle for a party, school fair or fun day? Here is what the PIPA tag means and how to check it in two minutes.
news.html:
If you've hired a bouncy castle before, you may have seen a small tag stitched onto it. That's usually a PIPA tag – and it's one of the simplest ways to check that an inflatable is safe to use.

What the tag proves

A PIPA tag shows that the inflatable has been inspected by a registered inspector against BS EN 14960, the European standard for inflatable play equipment, and that the test has been logged on the national PIPA database. Each tag has a unique number, so you can look up that exact inflatable online.

How to check it

  • Ask the hire company for the tag number before your event.
  • Look it up on pipa.org.uk.
  • Check that the photo matches what's delivered and that the last test was within the past year – inflatables need inspecting annually.

PIPA or ADIPS?

HSE guidance accepts either a numbered PIPA tag or an ADIPS Declaration of Compliance for play inflatables. ADIPS is the inspection scheme for fairground and amusement devices. Either way, you should also get written evidence of compliance and instructions for safe use.

What else to ask your supplier

  • Do you have public liability insurance, and can you send the certificate?
  • Will you send a risk assessment for my venue?
  • Who will supervise, and what are the user limits?
  • What happens if it's too windy on the day?

At JM Inflatable Hire we follow the PIPA scheme for our inflatables – read how we follow PIPA or ask us for the tag numbers on your quote.

news.title: Inflatable Hire Safety Checklist for Event Organisers
news.meta: A practical inflatable safety checklist for event organisers, schools and PTAs based on HSE guidance – PIPA tags, anchoring, wind limits, supervision and paperwork.
news.summary: Running a fun day, sports day or staff event with inflatables? Use this checklist, based on HSE guidance, to make sure everything is in order.
news.html:
Inflatables are one of the most popular attractions at fun days, fairs and corporate events – and with the right checks they're very safe. This checklist pulls together the main points from HSE guidance on bouncy castles and play inflatables.

Before you book

  • Inspection: ask for the PIPA tag number or ADIPS Declaration of Compliance for each inflatable, and check PIPA tags at pipa.org.uk.
  • Insurance: ask for the supplier's public liability insurance certificate.
  • Risk assessment: your venue or council may ask for the supplier's risk assessment and method statement.
  • Permission: parks and public spaces usually need event permission from the council or landowner.

The site

  • Choose level ground – guidance used by schools and PTAs suggests no more than a 5% slope.
  • Keep clear of overhead cables, trees, fences and other hazards, with space all round for safety mats.
  • Plan power: most blowers need a 13 amp socket, or ask about a generator.

On the day

  • Anchoring: all anchor points should be used. HSE guidance is a minimum of six anchor points, with steel stakes on grass, or ballast on hard surfaces where stakes can't be used.
  • Wind: inflatables must not be used in winds above 24mph (Force 5) – some have a lower limit – so wind speed should be measured during the event.
  • Mats: safety mats at the entrance so people can get on and off safely.
  • Supervision: an adult must supervise at all times and keep to the user limit for that inflatable.
  • Rules: no shoes, glasses, jewellery, food, drink or sharp objects; similar-sized users together.

If the weather turns

Stop play and get everyone off if wind or rain becomes a problem, then deflate safely. Have a plan B – a hall or marquee – for big events.

When you book with JM Inflatable Hire we follow the PIPA scheme, supply the paperwork and brief your supervisors – or add our operators for the day. See our school fun day and corporate fun day pages for ideas.

news.title: Wind and Weather: Why We Stop Inflatables Above 24mph
news.meta: Why inflatables must stop in winds above 24mph, what happens if it rains, and how JM Inflatable Hire plans for the British weather at your event.
news.summary: The British weather is the one thing we can't control. Here's how wind and rain affect inflatables, and how we plan for them.
news.html:
Wind is the biggest weather risk for any inflatable. That's why HSE guidance says inflatables must not be used in winds above 24mph – Force 5 on the Beaufort scale – and some inflatables have a lower limit set by the manufacturer.

What we do

  • Watch the forecast with you in the days before your event, and talk through options if strong winds are likely.
  • Measure the wind on site during set-up and keep an eye on it through the day.
  • Anchor every inflatable fully, using all its anchor points.
  • Stop play and deflate safely if the limit is reached. Your supervisor or our operator will clear the inflatable first.

What about rain?

Light rain doesn't usually stop play, but wet surfaces are slippery, so supervisors may pause it. Some of our castles have rain covers, and heavy rain means stopping for safety.

Plan B ideas

  • Check whether your venue has a sports hall or marquee with enough height.
  • Pick attractions that work indoors – many inflatable games and the rodeo bull do.
  • Agree timings so we can move things if needed.

Read more in our weather FAQs.
